builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Agentic Harness Engineering Beta: Requirement-Centered Evolution of Agent Harnesses
summary: Replaces single-agent harness evolution with benchmark-score selection by a requirement-centered loop: simulated users file issues over multiple turns, a team of agents implements generalizable changes, and changes merge only after verified requirement resolution and review. Costs are additional orchestration complexity, LLM calls for user simulation and multi-agent modification, and a human-style review gate, though the resulting harness itself reports 40.8% fewer tokens at inference. Can fail if simulated-user requirements diverge from real user needs on the reader's workload, if evolution overfits to the evaluation tasks despite the held-out protocol, or if the gains do not replicate on models other than those tested.
rationale: Improving the harness around existing API models fits constrained infrastructure, but the three-step evolution loop (simulated users, team-based modification, requirement-driven selection) must be validated on the reader's own tasks before production reliance.

claims.statement: Replaces single-agent harness evolution with benchmark-score selection by a requirement-centered loop: simulated users file issues over multiple turns, a team of agents implements generalizable changes, and changes merge only after verified requirement resolution and review. Costs are additional orchestration complexity, LLM calls for user simulation and multi-agent modification, and a human-style review gate, though the resulting harness itself reports 40.8% fewer tokens at inference. Can fail if simulated-user requirements diverge from real user needs on the reader's workload, if evolution overfits to the evaluation tasks despite the held-out protocol, or if the gains do not replicate on models other than those tested.
Raises held-out pass@1 from 21.9% to 33.3% while using 40.8% fewer tokens than the base harness; gains transfer to other models (15.8% and 5.3% pass@1 improvements) without further evolution.
